title: Per-callee delegation policy
description: The callee's delegation policy, stored as its OWN file at `.fuze/a2a-delegation.json`. Deliberately NOT a key inside the manifest's `a2a` block: contracts/a2a/v1's manifest-a2a-extension.schema.json sets additionalProperties:false on that block, so adding `delegation` there would make every adopting repo's manifest fail v1 validation. An extension that requires editing the frozen contract to adopt is a version, not an extension — a separate file is what keeps this additive. It classifies EVERY published skill; there is no default class and no wildcard that could supply one, so an unclassified skill is denied and a new skill cannot acquire the weakest rule in the system merely by being written.

extension.description: Pinned URI. A policy that does not name the extension it implements cannot be checked against the right rules.

authzBaseUrl.description: Base URL of FuzeFront's Security API for the Permit decision (/api/v1/security/authz/check). A product never calls Permit directly. Unreachable is DENY — there is no fail-open option.

skills.description: role key -> class. Every published skill MUST appear. Absence is DENY, never `delegable`.

additionalProperties.description: delegable = v1 behaviour, any allowlisted caller. principal-required = verified `sub` AND a Permit ALLOW for that subject. never-delegable = no principal reaches it via A2A regardless of `sub` (the machine-readable form of authz.md §7's reach_human and _base guardrails).

brokerable.description: actor reference -> the role keys that actor may BROKER. The second half of the intersection in spec.md §4: the subject cannot reach past this, no matter what Permit says about the subject. An actor absent here brokers nothing.

additionalProperties.description: Role keys. An empty array means this actor brokers nothing — which is a meaningful, explicit statement, unlike absence.
